{{Short description|Cryptographic micropayment system}}
'''Peppercoin''' is a [[cryptography|cryptographic]] system for processing [[micropayment]]s. '''Peppercoin Inc.''' was a company that offered services based on the peppercoin method.

The peppercoin system was developed by [[Silvio Micali]] and [[Ron Rivest]] and first presented at the RSA Conference in 2002<ref>S. Micali and R. L. Rivest. ''[http://citeseer.ist.psu.edu/micali02micropayments.html Micropayments revisited] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080226201037/http://citeseer.ist.psu.edu/micali02micropayments.html |date=2008-02-26 }}.'' In B. Preneel, editor,
Proc. Cryptography Track at RSA Conference 2002, pages 149–263. Springer,
2002. Lecture Notes in Computer Science No. 2271.</ref> (although it had not yet been named.) The core idea is to bill one randomly selected transaction a lump sum of money rather than bill each transaction a small amount. It uses "universal aggregation", which means that it aggregates transactions over users, merchants as well as [[payment service provider]]s. The random selection is cryptographically secure—it cannot be influenced by any of the parties. It is claimed to reduce the [[transaction cost]] per dollar from 27 cents to "well below 10 cents."<ref>{{cite web |title=2003 press release |url=http://www.peppercoin.com/press/pressreleases/2003/0929.shtml |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060316103522/http://www.peppercoin.com/press/pressreleases/2003/0929.shtml |archivedate=16 Mar 2006 |date=29 Sep 2003}}</ref>

Peppercoin, Inc. was a privately held company founded in late 2001 by Micali and Rivest based in [[Waltham, Massachusetts|Waltham, MA]]. It has secured about $15M in venture capital in two rounds of funding.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.peppercoin.com/company/history.shtml |title=Company history|website=Peppercoin.com|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20061015223403/http://www.peppercoin.com/company/history.shtml|archivedate=15 October 2006}}</ref><ref name="alarm">[http://www.thealarmclock.com/mt/archives/2007/04/micropayments_p.html Micro-payment's Peppercoin Bought Out] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080119122130/http://www.thealarmclock.com/mt/archives/2007/04/micropayments_p.html |date=January 19, 2008 }}</ref> Its services saw modest adoption.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.masshightech.com/stories/2005/03/28/daily9-Peppercoin-picked-by-Wurld-Media-for-P2P-payment-system.html |title=Peppercoin picked by Wurld Media for P2P payment system |access-date=2012-09-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120806212242/http://www.masshightech.com/stories/2005/03/28/daily9-Peppercoin-picked-by-Wurld-Media-for-P2P-payment-system.html |archive-date=2012-08-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bizjournals.com/boston/stories/2006/07/24/story10.html|title=Peppercoin scoops up customer for loyalty program|website=Boston Business Journal|access-date=2017-03-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302025822/http://www.bizjournals.com/boston/stories/2006/07/24/story10.html|archive-date=2017-03-02|url-status=live}}{{Subscription required}}</ref> Peppercoin collects 5-9% of transaction cost from the merchant.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://net.educause.edu/elements/attachments/rfi/rfi_2/Peppercoin_summary.pdf |title=Peppercoin, Inc. Response to the Request for Information By the Joint Committee of the Higher Education and Entertainment Communities Technology Task Force |access-date=2012-09-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111005044525/http://net.educause.edu/elements/attachments/rfi/rfi_2/Peppercoin_summary.pdf |archive-date=2011-10-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Peppercoin, Inc. was bought out in 2007 by Chockstone for an undisclosed amount.<ref name="alarm" />
